**Test image summary:** Field-level view of soybean plants with dead/dying lower canopy leaves (tan/yellow-brown, hanging limply) while upper canopy remains green and healthy. Classic lower-canopy-first progression pattern.

**Class-by-class comparison:**

- **SDS** (Soybean_Dise_251, 257): Interveinal chlorosis with distinct green veins; whole-plant shows widespread field yellowing — doesn't match the localized lower canopy die-off in test image
- **Brown_Stem_Rot** (Soybean_Dise_110): Leaf reference showed dramatic interveinal necrosis in foreground with green-canopy background — the whole-plant context is visually closest to the test image's dead lower leaves + green upper canopy
- **Septoria_brown_spot** (Soybean_Dise_107): Close-up of yellow leaf with small dark spots — doesn't match whole-plant perspective well
- **Phytophthora** (Soybean_Dise_24): Plants collapsing/dying in wet-soil patches — very different pattern
- **Soybean_rust** (Soybean_Dise_110): Lower canopy defoliation with bare stems visible — some similarity but upper canopy in test image is denser/healthier
- **Charcoal_Rot** (Soybean_Dise_47): Whole row/plant collapse — plants are more completely dead
- **Fusarium** (Soybean_Dise_33): Mostly green plants, subtle symptoms
- All leaf-spot diseases (Cercospora, Frogeye, Downy, Bacterial_Blight, Powdery, Bacterial_Pustule, Phyllosticta, SVNV, Bean_Pod_Mottle, Anthracnose): Close-up leaf patterns, don't match this whole-plant lower-canopy-death view

**Best match:** Brown_Stem_Rot — the reference showed a leaf with interveinal necrosis hanging in front of a green canopy background, closely matching the test image's pattern of dead lower leaves against a healthy green upper canopy. The KB description also matches: lower canopy leaf curling and death while upper canopy remains green.
